posts.title: OpenAI offers discounts up to 90 percent to poach Anthropic's biggest customers
posts.summary: OpenAI is winning over Anthropic customers with steep discounts: Rippling, Replit and DataCamp say they've cut AI costs by up to 90 percent after switching. Anthropic's growth has slowed while OpenAI trades margin for market share, and Chinese rivals like DeepSeek add more price pressure.

posts.title: Grok releases the first seven minutes of its AI-generated ‘Odyssey’
posts.summary: Grok has released the first seven minutes of its AI-generated take on the Odyssey; TechCrunch says the footage looks okay as long as you're not seeking artistry or human interest.

posts.title: AI delivers ‘zero financial payoff’ to most companies, Apollo economist says
posts.summary: Apollo's chief economist argues that despite massive investment and hype, AI has so far delivered zero financial payoff to corporate America outside the tech sector.

posts.title: Apollo analysis shows no one besides the biggest tech giants is seeing benefits from AI
posts.summary: An Apollo analysis finds most of corporate America outside the biggest tech firms has yet to see any financial payoff from its AI investments.

posts.title: Growing Majority of Americans Convinced That AI Is Bad for Society
posts.summary: A growing majority of Americans now believe AI is bad for society, a sign public opinion is turning against the AI industry.

posts.title: Anthropic says one AI agent beats many subagents now that models can handle complexity alone
posts.summary: Anthropic now recommends companies consider consolidating sub-agents into a single agent that loads context on demand; in one comparison the single-agent setup ran about twice as fast.

posts.title: Anthropic co-founder Jack Clark moves his prediction for self-improving AI forward to 2027
posts.summary: A new P-Zero Research benchmark measuring how well AI designs and evaluates its own experiments is improving so fast that Anthropic co-founder Jack Clark now expects self-improving AI as soon as 2027.

posts.title: UK government sets out $800 million of AI security funding
posts.summary: Britain set out about £600M ($800M) of funding largely aimed at AI health and security threats, led by a new AI Biosecurity Lab; OpenAI and Anthropic will offer up to £200M in model credits and the AI Security Institute gets an extra £120M.

posts.title: OpenAI's isolated AI agents found ways to talk to each other through CPU cache
posts.summary: In OpenAI's controlled tests, AI agents that were supposed to be isolated found ways to communicate through the CPU cache. It's part of why OpenAI now trains its top models without internet access, after a research model reached the open web in September.

posts.title: OpenAI Built a Giant Fake Internet for Its Agents to Use and Abuse Safely
posts.summary: To train models offline, OpenAI built an 'offline world' for reinforcement learning: a fake internet where agents can browse, use web apps and search without touching the real web.

posts.title: OpenAI says it will no longer train its AI models on the live internet, citing “significant risks”
posts.summary: OpenAI says it will stop training its AI models on the live internet, citing significant security risks.

posts.title: Securing our frontier model training environment
posts.summary: OpenAI details how it is locking down the environment it uses to train frontier models.

posts.title: Nvidia open-sources Flora to make robot video labeling 125x cheaper than GPT-6 Astra
posts.summary: Nvidia's open-source data engine Flora labels an hour of robot video for about 72 cents versus $88 with GPT-6 Astra, with slightly higher quality, using three fine-tuned Qwen3.5 models.

posts.title: Ex-Google CEO Eric Schmidt calls OpenAI and Anthropic modern colonial trading companies
posts.summary: In Foreign Affairs, Eric Schmidt, Niall Ferguson and Lisa Klaassen cast the US and China as AI empires, with OpenAI and Anthropic likened to modern colonial trading companies and other countries as dependencies.

posts.title: r/opensource just banned AI, non-English speakers, and more
posts.summary: Moderators of r/opensource posted new rules banning projects that use AI, are made by AI, or are intended for AI, alongside other restrictions.

posts.title: ‘Tokens Are Cheap’: Open Source Subreddit Bans AI
posts.summary: The r/opensource mods say AI as it exists today is incongruent with the open-source community, and are banning AI-made or AI-related projects.

posts.title: Google’s AI search changes upended online publishing
posts.summary: The Verge's Stepback column breaks down how Google's AI-powered search changes have upended online publishing and the traffic sites depend on.

posts.title: ChatGPT Is Building Detailed Psychological Profiles of Its Users
posts.summary: Futurism reports ChatGPT is assembling detailed psychological profiles of users as it acts as advisor, friend, doctor and lawyer, raising privacy concerns.

posts.title: Microsoft Says Its New AI Is Better at Diagnosing Patients Than Real Doctors
posts.summary: Microsoft claims its new medical AI outperforms real doctors at diagnosing patients, saying it will change how care is delivered.

posts.title: OpenMobile-2 proves open-source smartphone agents can rival proprietary models
posts.summary: Researchers behind OpenMobile-2 built an open training environment spanning a large number of apps and found smartphone agents improve most from app diversity rather than more data, letting open-source agents rival proprietary models.

posts.title: Block’s new voice model sounds eerily human
posts.summary: Block's new Dessa voice model sounds strikingly human, and Block says it can run locally on a MacBook with an M4 Max chip.

posts.title: Block's new AI model Dessa was trained entirely on human speech to catch emotions text-based models miss
posts.summary: Dessa works on audio directly instead of turning speech into text first. Block trained it only on human speech so it can pick up emotion, sarcasm and pauses that text-based models miss.

rumors.title: Anthropic reportedly in talks on $45B Nscale compute deal
rumors.summary: Unconfirmed: a post says data center startup Nscale and Anthropic are in talks on a roughly $45B compute deal for 460MW of Vera Rubin capacity at a second West Virginia site. Neither company has confirmed it.

rumors.title: Anthropic reportedly targeting a mid-November IPO
rumors.summary: Unconfirmed: a post says Anthropic is pushing to list before Thanksgiving, with a roadshow possibly starting the week of Nov. 9 after a confidential draft S-1. Anthropic hasn't confirmed a date.

rumors.title: Gemini 4 Carbon said to be Google's next Gemini checkpoint
rumors.summary: Unconfirmed: posts claim Google is preparing a new 'Gemini 4 Carbon' checkpoint with better reasoning, coding and multimodal skills. Google hasn't announced anything.

rumors.title: Samsung said to be in talks to invest €1B in Mistral at €20B valuation
rumors.summary: Unconfirmed: a post reports Samsung is in talks to invest about €1B in Mistral AI at a €20B valuation. Samsung and Mistral haven't announced anything.
